response.sql:
WITH ratio_data AS (
  SELECT
    order_item_id,
    CASE
      WHEN product_price IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost != 0
      THEN product_price / derived_total_cost
      ELSE NULL
    END AS ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
),
per_item_stats AS (
  SELECT
    order_item_id,
    AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio,
    COUNT(*) AS line_item_count
  FROM ratio_data
  GROUP BY order_item_id
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio,
  AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item
FROM per_item_stats
WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: A ratio is 'missing' when product_price or derived_total_cost is NULL, or derived_total_cost is 0 (division by zero). These rows are excluded from per-item average calculations.
Order items with no valid ratios (all invoice line items have missing ratios) are excluded from the final aggregation, as implied by 'ignoring missing ones'.
The count of invoice line items per order item includes all line items (even those with missing/null ratios), not just those with calculable ratios.

alternatives.interpretation: 'How many invoice line items it has' could mean only those with valid (non-null) ratios, not the total count. This would change COUNT(*) to COUNT(ratio) in the per-item-stats step.
